questions.q: Why does the SR-5 backtest engine use a C++ core (sr5_fast) alongside Python?
options: C++ is required to call pandas
The rolling cross-sectional z-score and the purged walk-forward retrain loop run thousands of times and need the speed
Python cannot read Parquet files
Ridge regression only has a C++ implementation
questions.explain: Two loops — the rolling cross-sectional z-score and the walk-forward retraining loop — run thousands of times across the 2007–2025 backtest, so they're pushed into a C++17 core for speed.

questions.q: What role does pybind11 play in the SR-5 architecture?
options: It converts Python code into C++ automatically
It exposes the C++ sr5_fast functions so they can be called directly from Python as ordinary imports
It is a visualization library for the equity curve
It replaces pandas for data loading
questions.explain: pybind11 wraps the C++ sr5_fast module so Python code can call its functions, like rolling_zscore, exactly like any other Python function.

questions.q: In the vectorized weekly backtest loop, what is the one governing discipline that prevents lookahead?
options: Using only data available at or before each Friday's rebalance to make that week's decision (point-in-time alignment)
Running the loop in C++ instead of Python
Recomputing Ridge from scratch every day
Always using the full-sample average return
questions.explain: Point-in-time alignment means nothing dated after the rebalance Friday can influence that Friday's decision — the backtest-engine-level version of the embargo and execution-lag discipline from earlier lessons.

questions.q: Which three outputs does every SR-5 backtest run produce, saved to Parquet?
options: Equity curve, holdings log, and turnover
Sharpe ratio, VaR, and CVaR only
Raw OHLCV data, VIX level, and SPY price
Feature importances, confusion matrix, and ROC curve
questions.explain: Every run writes an equity curve, a holdings log (positions at every rebalance date), and a turnover series to Parquet.

questions.q: Why does turnover matter beyond this lesson?
options: It has no further use once the backtest runs
It's the number that directly drives the transaction-cost analysis in Lesson 11
It determines the VIX regime
It replaces the Information Coefficient as the model's skill metric
questions.explain: Turnover — how much of the book trades each rebalance — is the key driver of the cost analysis covered in Lesson 11.
